answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with bonded identity: every agent locks a refundable stake before transacting, like a falcon tethered to its perch by a deposit it loses if it misbehaves. A walnut-sized bond per identity is cheap for one honest agent but ruinous for an attacker spinning up ten thousand sock puppets, since each fake costs real capital. When two identities are proven to share one operator, both bonds are slashed and the identities burned, so the comet of cheap fake accounts fizzles out: creating identities no longer scales for free.
